topPRs.title: kona-node,op-reth,op-batcher: multi-blocks PoC (up to max_multi_blocks blocks per block time)
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
**Draft / PoC, work in progress — CI feedback only for now.**

Multi-blocks: keep `block_time`, allow the sequencer to build up to `max_multi_blocks` L2 blocks sharing one timestamp after a feature timestamp `multi_block_time` (≥ Karst, not a hardfork). Sealing policy is the builder's choice; consensus only bounds the group size. Chain consistency is parent-hash linkage.

Scope of the PoC: kona-node (sequencer + derivation), op-reth (EL), op-batcher (span batch v2), op-devstack + acceptance tests on a kona-node/op-reth-only devnet. op-node keeps rejecting span batch v2; interop, proofs, flashblocks and registry support are out of scope.

Landed so far (one commit per workstream):
- op-reth: `ts == parent.ts` accepted iff siblings are allowed at `ts`; builder seal policy flags; `engine_awaitPayloadReadyV1`
- kona: `multi_block_time`/`max_multi_blocks` config; `BatchType::SpanV2` = Delta span + `same_ts_bits` (bit 0 = sibling of the span's parent, so groups may straddle spans/channels)
- Go: rollup/deploy config, span batch v2 codec + `SpanChannelOut` switch, devstack options and DSL helpers, shared golden vectors

Still to come: kona derivation validity, kona sequencer slot loop, acceptance tests.

Judgement calls worth a look:
- the `min-build-time` policy only seals a payload that holds ≥ 1 user tx, so an idle sequencer still makes one block per block time
- straddling groups across span batches/channels is allowed (bit 0), instead of forcing the batcher to keep groups atomic across L1-driven channel closes
- `siblings_allowed` is false at *every* configured fork activation timestamp, which keeps the timestamp-only `is_first_<fork>_block` predicates correct for forks scheduled after activation

topPRs.title: op-challenger: delete withdrawal proofs invalidated by challenger wins
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Adrian Sutton** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BTT5DGHA4/p1787791642391549?thread_ts=1787791642.391549&cid=C0BTT5DGHA4)_

Stacks on #22669.

**Before:** #22669 makes `deleteProvenWithdrawal` permissionless once the game a withdrawal was proven against resolves as `CHALLENGER_WINS`, but nothing calls it. Those proofs can never finalize, yet they stay in `provenWithdrawals` and keep counting toward `numProofSubmitters`, so anything reading the portal still sees a live proof against an invalid game.

**After:** op-challenger deletes them automatically. The feature is off unless `--optimism-portal-address` is set; when it is, the challenger logs once at startup and clears invalidated proofs on every L1 head, alongside bond claiming.

**How:** A new `game/withdrawals` scheduler runs beside the bond claimer and gets the same games list. For each game that resolved `CHALLENGER_WINS` it filters `WithdrawalProvenExtension1` logs from the game's `l1Head` block, batch-reads `provenWithdrawals` for the pairs it finds, and sends a delete for each one still recorded against that game. Deleted rows read back with a zero timestamp, which makes this idempotent; an in-memory per-game cursor keeps later heads to the new blocks only.

**For reviewers:** anyone can prove many cheap withdrawals against a game the challenger will win, making the challenger pay unrewarded gas to delete them all — hence off unless the portal address is set, and capped at 100 deletes per game per head. Unit tests only, no e2e or action-test coverage.

topPRs.title: op-alt-da!: remove Alt-DA support
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
Removes Alt-DA runtime, deployment, contracts, packaging, tests, and active documentation. Legacy configurations now fail closed, and retired docs URLs redirect to supported Ethereum DA guidance.

BREAKING CHANGE: Alt-DA chains must migrate batch submission to Ethereum calldata or blobs before upgrading.

Tests: Go/Rust/Solidity lint and targeted tests; docs and CI validators.

topPRs.title: op-devstack: faithful sequencer-state persistence for supernode invalidation testing
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Description

Makes supernode VN sequencer-state behavior faithful to production — in the VN factory itself and in the devstack harness — so the invalidation acceptance tests exercise real recovery behavior. Split out from #21951.

> **Stack** (bottom → top): #21991 (gating fix) → **this PR** → #21993 (acceptance-test repro).

### Why

The supernode invalidation acceptance tests were silently self-healing, so they could not catch real recovery bugs — including the unsafe-sync re-adoption livelock fixed in #21991. The masking mechanism, spelled out:

1. **Old topology**: a light CL in ELSync mode cannot produce block 1 (#21164), so the light-sequencer tests bootstrapped the chain by having the **supernode VN sequence first**, then hand off to the light CL. After the handoff the VN was stopped via admin RPC and was supposed to stay a passive follower forever.
2. **But "stopped" never survived a restart**: the devstack VN config used no-op config persistence, and the VN factory never called `LoadPersisted` anyway — so the stop existed only in the running process.
3. **Invalidation recovery restarts every VN** (op-node graceful shutdown — which dutifully persists `sequencer.stopped=true`… into the no-op store).
4. **The restarted VN boots from its static config** — sequencer enabled, not stopped — and the retired bootstrap sequencer comes back to life. At that moment the chain has **two active sequencers simultaneously**: the light CL (the intended one) and the resurrected VN.
5. **The resurrected VN immediately builds valid blocks on the supernode's own post-invalidation state** (the deposits-only replacement branch), so the chain visibly "recovers" within seconds — regardless of whether invalidation recovery actually works. Any assertion of the form "chain healthy after invalidation" passed vacuously; the re-adoption livelock was invisible.

This PR closes every link in that chain: the factory honors persisted state (commit 1), devstack persists it for real (commit 3), the tests explicitly play the operator when sequencing *should* resume (commit 5), and the bootstrap-handoff topology is removed outright in favor of production wiring (commits 6–7). Separately, the old bootstrap wiring contained a latent recovery livelock of its own (see commit 7).

### Commits

1. **`op-supernode: honor persisted sequencer state in VN factory`** — the one production change in this PR. The VN factory builds its op-node config programmatically and bypasses the op-node CLI entrypoint (`op-node/service.go`), which is where `cfg.LoadPersisted` applies persisted sequencer state — so VNs silently ignored it, and a VN restart re-enabled sequencing that an operator (`admin_stopSequencer`) or an invalidation rewind had stopped. Now the factory calls `LoadPersisted`, matching op-node restart semantics: an operator stop survives restarts; re-enabling requires an explicit `admin_startSequencer`. No-op unless the VN is sequencer-enabled with active config persistence and a recorded state.
2. **`op-supernode: document sequencing disabled after invalidation rewind`** — comment-only. The rewind restarts every VN through op-node's graceful shutdown, which persists `sequencer.stopped=true`; with the commit above, restarted VNs honor that state, so a supernode that was actively sequencing exits invalidation recovery with sequencing disabled until an explicit operator/conductor start — intentional: internal restarts must not silently resurrect a sequencer.
3. **`op-devstack: use real config persistence for supernode VNs`** — persisted sequencer state (stopped/started) now survives VN restarts in tests the same way it does in production.
4. **`op-devstack: fix goimports formatting in supernode runtime`** — formatting only.
5. **`op-acceptance-tests: re-enable sequencing after invalidation rewind`** — the invalidation rewind leaves every VN with sequencing disabled (now that persisted state is honored). The virtual-sequencer tests play the operator: once the reset is detected, re-enable sequencing on both chains via admin RPC. The helper is guarded by `SequencerActive`, so light-sequencer topologies — whose sequencing CLs never restart — are untouched. No assertions added, removed, or weakened.
6. **`op-devstack: sequence light CLs from genesis with CLSync`** — an ELSync CL cannot produce block 1: it only leaves `willStartEL` on the first network payload, which as sole sequencer it is itself supposed to produce (#21164). Light sequencer CLs now boot with CLSync when sequencing from genesis; VN-bootstrap mode keeps ELSync for the pre-handoff sync from the VN, so the `follow_l2` bootstrap tests are unaffected.
7. **`op-acceptance-tests: start light sequencers from genesis`** — the light invalid-message test drops the VN-sequencer bootstrap + handoff entirely: light CLs sequence from genesis with the batcher following them, matching production wiring (batchers point at the light sequencer nodes, not the supernode). This also removes a recovery livelock latent in the old bootstrap wiring: a batcher pinned to the supernode VN starves during invalidation recovery — its frozen view produces no new batches, so finality can never advance past the denied height.

### Tests

Existing invalidation suite validated against the full stack: `TestSupernodeInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`, `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`, `TestSupernodeInteropRPCGatedDuringReorg`, `TestSupernodeResyncSchedulesAtActivation_PreActivation`.

### Metadata

- Split from #21951

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: add permissionless deleteProvenWithdrawal to OptimismPortal2
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Adrian Sutton, Matt Solomon** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BTT5DGHA4/p1787791642391549?thread_ts=1787791642.391549&cid=C0BTT5DGHA4)_

**Before:** A withdrawal proven against a dispute game that later resolved `CHALLENGER_WINS`, or that was blacklisted, stays in `provenWithdrawals` forever. The record can never finalize, but nothing can clear it, so the portal accumulates dead state and monitoring gets no on-chain signal that a proof has been abandoned.

**After:** `deleteProvenWithdrawal(bytes32 _withdrawalHash, address _proofSubmitter)` lets anyone delete such a record and emits `WithdrawalProofDeleted`. No access control is needed: both conditions are permanent and independently verifiable on-chain, so the caller has no discretion and can only remove state that was already unusable. Retired and non-respected games are deliberately out of scope.

**How:** The function loads the proof, reverts `OptimismPortal_Unproven` if it was never submitted, requires the recorded game to be `CHALLENGER_WINS` or blacklisted in the `AnchorStateRegistry`, then deletes the entry. It leaves `finalizedWithdrawals` untouched so replay protection still holds, and leaves the append-only `proofSubmitters` entry in place — that stale entry now points at a zeroed record, which `checkWithdrawal` already rejects as unproven. Semver bumped to 5.9.0.
